subject: Order form: third-party trigger, SLA carveout & evidence lifecycle
messages:
From: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@clearsight.io>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@clearsight.io>
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order form question — indemnity triggers and SLA carveout

Hi Rachel,

Quick follow up from procurement: our legal team flagged the indemnity language in the order form around third-party IP claims. They want clarity on two items before we sign:

1) Trigger: what constitutes a covered "third-party claim" when the alleged infringement arises from model output versus customer-supplied data?
2) SLA carveout: if a takedown request or claim requires immediate investigation that impacts availability, will Redwood accept a temporary SLA exception and provide an evidence preservation plan?

We can sign if there is a narrow carveout for availability SLOs tied to reasonable investigation windows, and an evidence-preservation checklist that our ops can follow. Can you share proposed language or a short mutual action plan?

Thanks — want to close this this week.

— Sarah
Sarah Nguyen
Head of Procurement, ClearSight Analytics

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Order form question — indemnity triggers and SLA carveout

Kimberly / Ben — forwarding a short procurement ask from ClearSight. Key asks: (1) define what triggers coverage when claim relates to model output vs customer data, and (2) agree an availability/SLA exception tied to investigation plus an evidence-preservation plan.

We don't want an open-ended SLA carveout that undermines our SLOs for paying customers. Proposed approach:
- Keep IP indemnity limited to third-party claims alleging infringement by our delivered model artifacts or licensed components (not downstream outputs), while offering a narrow defense cooperation process for alleged output-infringement (e.g., remediation assistance, temporary content block).
- Accept a time-bound SLA exception for availability when an active CS claim is under investigation, with defined caps (e.g., 72hr investigation window, documented mitigation steps, and fallback model variant).
- Provide an evidence-preservation checklist (ops steps + contact points) that we attach as an exhibit to the order form.

Can you draft redline language and an ops checklist (attachable)? I can use Ben to route procurement approvals. They want to close this week.

Thanks,
Rachel
Rachel Kim | Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 11:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Order form question — indemnity triggers and SLA carveout

Rachel / Ben — see attached redline (CS_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf) and an evidence-preservation checklist (evidence-preservation-checklist.xlsx). High-level notes:

1) Trigger language
- Drafted a carve-in: Redwood will defend/reimburse for third-party claims that the Redwood-delivered software or model code (i.e., the model weights, binaries, or licensed components we ship) infringes a third party's intellectual property.
- For claims based on model outputs (text, code, images), proposed treatment: mutual cooperation + remediation assistance rather than classic indemnity. If the claimed infringement is traceable to customer-supplied data or prompts, ClearSight would retain responsibility.

2) SLA carveout and evidence preservation
- We can accept a narrow SLA exception: if Redwood reasonably determines that an active third-party claim necessitates immediate mitigation that affects availability, Redwood may temporarily suspend affected endpoints for up to 72 hours while we investigate. We will notify the customer within 4 hours of action and provide daily status updates during the suspension.
- Exceptions beyond 72 hours require executive approval and will trigger a customer credit schedule capped at the monthly service fee prorated for downtime beyond the window.
- Evidence-preservation checklist: contains steps for capturing request/response logs, KV cache snapshots, model variant identifiers, and a named point-of-contact at Redwood. It also includes a documented transfer method (secure S3 presigned link) and retention terms (90 days by default, extendable by agreement).

3) Risk & commercial compromise
- To protect Redwood, recommend: (a) mutual indemnity for gross negligence only for output claims, or (b) a reimbursement cap equal to the fees paid for the affected service year for output-based remediation. We included both as options in the redline.

If you want, I can prepare two bracketed options for the customer (option A = mutual cooperation + no indemnity for output; option B = limited indemnity with annual cap). Ben, can you confirm if discounts were already authorized for this opportunity (affects cap proposals)?

Attached: CS_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf (redline with bracketed options), evidence-preservation-checklist.xlsx (ops checklist).

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@clearsight.io>
Cc: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@clearsight.io>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form question — indemnity triggers and SLA carveout

Hi Sarah — thanks, appreciate the quick turnaround. Attaching a short redline and an evidence-preservation checklist for your team to review. High points:

- Trigger: Redwood will accept indemnity/defense for third-party claims alleging infringement by Redwood-delivered model binaries or licensed components.
- Model output: for alleged infringement tied to model output, we propose cooperation + remediation assistance; we included an optional limited indemnity with an annual cap as a compromise path (see bracketed options in the redline).
- SLA: we will accept a time-limited SLA exception while investigating an active claim (up to 72 hours) with 4-hour notice to you and daily updates. Any extension needs executive sign-off and is subject to a capped credit schedule.
- Evidence plan: checklist includes the exact logs and snapshots we will collect plus instructions for secure transfer. Redwood will keep the preserved evidence for 90 days unless you request longer retention.

Next steps:
1) Please review the attached redline and check which bracketed option you prefer for model-output claims (Option A: cooperation only; Option B: limited indemnity with cap).
2) Sign the attached short exhibit (evidence checklist) or propose edits.
3) If you pick Option B, let me know and I will route for expedited exec approval and provide the cap numbers.

I've included Kimberly on the cc for any legal specifics. If you prefer a quick call to finish this, I can schedule one this afternoon.

DocuSign link (prepped if you accept option A and checklist): https://www.docusign.com/link/clearsight-orderform-v3

Thanks — aiming to complete signature by EOD Friday.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
